body: @yatindra does this happen with any `@Singleton` bean or just gRPC related ones?

@tsegismont for me it happens for any `@Singleton` if `quarkus-grpc` is in classpath. I have another module which also has a repository with `PgPool` but in a pure JSON REST app, I created a `@Singleton` there and was able to inject `PgPool`.
Thank you @yatindra . cc @cescoffier this is useful info

FYI, a gRPC service is just a singleton bean, nothing else. 
Maybe when we create the instance, we need to pass some "context"

When exactly is the `@Singleton` gRPC bean instantiated? It's very likely that the `PgPoolProducer` is not initialized yet at that moment and so the [producer returns null](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/reactive-pg-client/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/reactive/pg/client/runtime/PgPoolProducer.java#L37-L41).

@yatindra Does it happen only with the PG Pool or with any bean?

I was able to inject an application scoped bean in a bindable service.

The gRPC server instantiates the services during the startup - it might be too early. 

The instances are created there:
https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/grpc/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/grpc/runtime/GrpcServerRecorder.java#L227

It seems that we only guarantee that `PgPoolProducer` is initialized before the `StartupEvent` is fired. The problem is that we can't add the `PgPoolBuildItem` dependency to the `io.quarkus.grpc.deployment.GrpcServerProcessor.build()` build step. We could try to transform the `PgPoolProducer` into a synthetic bean that does not require initialization (preferred solution) or try to find another kind of "barrier".
